Feed-Backward Reconstruction is a fundamental technique in signal processing and computer graphics for resampling data.
It is based on the principle of convolution, where the output is the weighted sum of input samples.
It is widely used in image processing, texture mapping, and volume rendering pipelines where high-quality reconstruction is required.
